subject: Covariates on phi parameter in gpcount

messages.author: 5efaad54fa09a2ad
messages.subject: Covariates on phi parameter in gpcount
parts:
Hi unmarked users--

I'm having trouble running some temporary emigration models using gpcount. To test it out, I'm starting by analyzing 2 seasons of data. Each season consists of 5 sampling periods, and I'm assuming the time frame is short enough to have demographic closure. I'm working with terrestrial salamanders, which move back-and-forth vertically from the ground surface to underground retreats, and we know this movement is related to weather variables, such as recent rainfall. In the help for gpcount, it says "This model is also applicable to sampling designs in which the local population size is closed during the J repeated counts, and availability is related to factors such as the probability of vocalizing. In this case, density can be estimated by M(i)/plotArea." My interpretation is that instead of "probability of vocalizing," I have "probability of being on the surface." 

Here is my code for creating the frame...

y.2011.umf <- unmarkedFrameGPC(y=counts,
                               siteCovs=data.frame(lfi=lfi.z, tsi=tsi.z, slope=slope.z, 
                                                   par=par.z, aw=aw.z, base=base.z, basal=basal.z, 
                                                   aspect=aspect.z, site=site.z),
                               obsCovs=data.frame(date=dates, wco=woodyco, soiltemp=temp, timeday=timeday, 
                                                  since25=rain25, litter=litter, rocks=rocks),
                               yearlySiteCovs=list(season=seasons),
                               numPrimary=2)

And a few models I've run (or tried to run)...

modA <- gpcount(~1, ~1, ~1, y.2011.umf, K=50, control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=1))
modB <- gpcount(~1, ~1, ~since25, y.2011.umf, K=50, control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=1))
modC <- gpcount(~1, ~site, ~1, y.2011.umf, K=50, control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=1))
modD <- gpcount(~1, ~since25, ~1, y.2011.umf, K=50, control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=1))

The issue is with model D. A, B, and C run with seemingly no problem. When I try to run D, I get this error:

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'since25' not found

In Richard's paper it says that variation in phi can be modeled as a function of both plot- and survey-specific covariates, but do they have to be specified in different ways if they are going to be modifying phi vs p? Since my model B runs, I know that 'since25' is indeed there, but it seems like it can't find it when it's modifying phi. Also, model C runs, so I know that site covariates can modify phi. 

Anyone have experience with gpcount and have ideas? Or similar issues? Thanks for any insights.

parts:
Hi Katie,

I agree that the model is applicable to your data... don't know why I referenced "vocalizations" in the help page.

You can't model phi as a function of "obsCovs", only "siteCovs" or "yearlySiteCovs". The reason is that local abundance isn't allowed to change within secondary periods. 

Richard
